summary.tldr: Creates the Employment Insurance Council and sets out how it advises the Employment Insurance Commission on employment insurance matters.
what_it_does: Establishes the Employment Insurance Council as an advisory council that can give advice and recommendations to the Commission on its own initiative or when asked.
Requires the Council to have at least 12 members, split equally between worker and employer organisations, with the workers' and employers' commissioners as co-chairs.
Lets the Council invite outside people to meetings or working groups, issue public opinions, and prepare reports that can be tabled in Parliament.
Allows the Council to include observers from provincial and territorial governments and Indigenous representatives, and requires it to meet at least three times a year.
Adds the Council to the Employment Insurance Act and lets the Commission seek its advice on any matter related to its powers and functions.
summary.background: The bill amends the Department of Employment and Social Development Act and the Employment Insurance Act. It adds a new part on the Employment Insurance Council and a new role for the Council in the Employment Insurance Act.
